title: Dark-Higgs-mediated massive-vector scattering gives a separate SIDM candidate

source_evidence.locator: Sec.II.A; Sec.IV.B Eq.(17); Appendix VI.A-B Eqs.(18)-(26); Figs.4-6

assumptions: A separate U1(1) breaking supplies massive vector alpha and light radial mediator h1; vector abundance/stability and production remain to be established.
Tree-level t/u channels and source identical-particle angular weighting; massive effective cubic g, not dimensionless gauge g1.
Source plotted-relative-velocity convention and identical-particle normalization must be resolved before interpreting numeric cross sections.
predictions: Author plots for m_alpha=1 GeV, m_h1=1 MeV and effective g bare number 0.0175 show reduced transfer scattering at higher plotted speed.
Momentum-transfer weighting 1-|cos theta| suppresses forward/backward contributions; this is distinct from a generic total scattering cross section.
Possible galactic cores and compatibility with cluster bounds are future conditional consequences; no halo profile or abundance result follows from the curves alone.
